Implement a feature on the Nxeon platform (Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Prisma + Postgres + Tailwind). Work ONLY inside your isolated worktree **/opt/nxeon-wt-idea-gamepanel/** — a full copy of the repo with node_modules + .env already symlinked. ALL Edit/Write use absolute paths under that dir. NEVER edit /opt/nxeon. `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-idea-gamepanel` for shell. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and fix all type errors. Do NOT `npm run build`, do NOT deploy, do NOT restart services.

CARD — "Game server hosting panel" — a TOTAL OVERHAUL (not a reskin): a premium per-game-server management panel. First Read the design mockup: /opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/cmsx7wo1s003nhlzz0bavlpiy/b91014846cede1ab4e6209bb.png

Build (from the card):
- PERSISTENT server header always visible: "Rust Server #1 · Online · 24/100 Players · 32% CPU · 5.2/8 GB · 18.4/50 GB" with Connect / Restart / Stop always available.
- Per-server TABS: Overview (status, IP/port, players, CPU/RAM/disk, uptime, quick restart/stop/kill, live resource graphs), Console (live terminal, command input, search, clear, auto-scroll, save/download logs), Files (full manager: upload/download, create, rename, edit config, permissions, drag&drop), Mods, Plugins, Backups (auto+manual, restore, download, schedule, retention), Players (online, history, bans, whitelist, OP/admin, stats), Settings (name, version, startup params, env vars, config, auto-restart, crash recovery, scheduled tasks, network), Activity (events, logins, config changes, mod installs, backups, staff actions).
- DIFFERENTIATOR = "Mod Store": make Mods feel like an App Store — mod cards (name, ⭐ rating, install count, compatibility, Install); click → detail (description, screenshots, versions, requirements, dependencies, compatibility, reviews, changelog); Install → select version → confirm → auto-deps → restart if needed.
- "Build with AI" inside the game server ("Configure my Rust server for PvP", "Install a balanced mod pack", "Optimize for 100 players").
VISUAL: dark navy/black + electric blue/purple gradients, glass panels, thin borders, glowing status indicators, animated graphs, restrained neon. Make it SPACIOUS and premium — less crowded than the raw mockup.

FIRST explore the existing code (in your worktree): grep for gameVariant/gameConfig, the current game-server management pages, `lib/actions-*` (server lifecycle, console, files), and the mod manager models `GameMod`/`ServerMod` + their actions/seed data. REUSE existing server actions, console/file-manager/mod components, and the portal shell + design-system components. Wire to REAL backend where it exists; stub ONLY genuine gaps and clearly label + list them.

SCOPE (4 sibling agents run in parallel on other cards): ONLY the individual game-server MANAGEMENT panel + tabs + header. Do NOT touch the marketing carousel, deploy wizard, pricing, or landing pages.

RETURN (final text = DATA, not a user message): (1) files added/changed, 1 line each; (2) fully-wired vs stubbed; (3) how to test each tab (route + steps); (4) follow-ups/risks. No preamble.

## Summary

Built a dedicated premium game-server management panel that replaces the generic VPS tab shell for game servers only (VPS path untouched). It renders whenever `osTemplate.family ∈ GAME_FAMILIES`.

### (1) Files added / changed
- `components/customer/gamepanel/types.ts` — shared `GameHeaderData` / `PanelTab` types (no server imports).
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GamePanelHeader.tsx` — persistent glass vitals header: glowing status, players/CPU/RAM/disk with animated sparklines, Connect (copy) / Restart / Stop wired to `gamePower`; polls `/api/metrics` for graph shape.
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GameServerPanel.tsx` — client shell: sticky header + tab strip (Overview, Console, Files, Mods, Plugins, Backups, Players, Settings, Activity), `?tab=` deep-links.
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GameOverview.tsx` — server-info grid, resource meters, quick-actions (tab jumps), embedded `MetricsPanel` + real `DiskUsageChart`, live players peek, Build-with-AI.
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GameConsole.tsx` — live terminal: log tail + command input (`getGameLogs`/`sendGameCommand`), search filter, clear, auto-scroll toggle, download logs, power buttons.
- `components/customer/gamepanel/ModStore.tsx` — App-Store mod browser: cards (⭐/installs/compat/Install), detail drawer (screenshots, versions, deps, reviews, changelog), version→confirm install flow; `scope="plugins"` reframes to loader plugins.
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GamePlayers.tsx` — Online (list + kick/ban) plus History/Bans/Whitelist/Operators sub-tabs.
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GameBuildAI.tsx` — in-server AI assistant with game preset prompts, wired to `submitBuild`/`approveBuild`/`rejectBuild` + `/api/claude/[id]` polling.
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GameSchedules.tsx` — scheduled auto-restarts CRUD.
- `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` — added `node: true` include; early game-server branch that computes header data (connect address, players max, cpu/ram/disk, uptime, next-restart from soonest `GameSchedule`) and renders `<GameServerPanel>` with Files/Backups/Settings/Activity slots; composed the Settings panel (rename, `GameSettings`, `GameAutoUpdate`, schedules, startup/network cards).

### (2) Fully wired vs stubbed
- **Fully wired (real backend):** power (Connect/Restart/Stop/console power), live console logs + RCON commands, players online + kick/ban, Mods/Plugins install/uninstall (`GAME_MOD_SYNC`), scheduled restarts CRUD, game config (`GameSettings`), auto-update, Files (existing `FileManager`), Backups (existing image-backup tab: schedule/retention/create/restore), Activity (job timeline), Build-with-AI (existing Claude pipeline), CPU/RAM/disk graphs (`MetricsPanel`/`DiskUsageChart`). SANDBOX returns synthetic players/logs as before.
- **Stubbed & clearly labelled:** Mod Store detail meta — star rating, install counts, screenshots, version history, reviews, changelog (deterministic from slug; `GameMod` has no such columns) and the install version dropdown (installer always applies latest compatible; labelled). Players History/Bans/Whitelist/Operators ("coming soon" cards). Settings "Startup, environment & crash recovery" and header **Disk-used** figure (live per-VM disk-used isn't in the cheap status call — header shows capacity, Overview shows the real `DiskUsageChart`). Network throughput shows `—` (cumulative bytes, not a rate).

### (3) How to test — route `/dashboard/servers/<gameServerId>` (a server whose OS template family is a game, e.g. Rust/Minecraft)
- **Header:** always visible; copy Connect, Restart/Stop (needs RUNNING); sparklines animate.
- **Overview** (`?tab=overview`): info grid + resource meters + graphs + players peek; quick-action buttons jump tabs; Build-with-AI presets fill the box.
- **Console** (`?tab=console`): start/restart/stop; type a command → Send; use search, Auto-scroll, Clear, Download.
- **Files** (`?tab=files`): file manager (RUNNING-gated).
- **Mods** (`?tab=mods`): search/category/sort, Browse↔Installed toggle, click a card → detail drawer → pick version → Install → Confirm; Uninstall installed.
- **Plugins** (`?tab=plugins`): same store scoped to plugin categories.
- **Backups** (`?tab=backups`): schedule/retention/create/restore.
- **Players** (`?tab=players`): Online list + Kick/Ban; other sub-tabs show labelled placeholders.
- **Settings** (`?tab=settings`): rename, game options, auto-update, add/pause/remove restart schedule.
- **Activity** (`?tab=activity`): lifecycle timeline.

### (4) Follow-ups / risks
- **Mod Store storefront data is genuine gap:** add `rating`, `installCount`, `screenshots`, `versions`, `dependencies`, `reviews`, `changelog` to `GameMod` (and per-version install to the worker) to replace the slug-derived placeholders and make the version pin real.
- **Disk-used & network rate** need a lightweight live source for the header (currently capacity-only / `—`); the real disk chart is on Overview.
- **Players sub-views** (history/bans/whitelist/OP) need persistence + worker/RCON support.
- **Build-with-AI** requires a funded Anthropic key (BYOK gate in `submitBuild`) — otherwise it returns the "add your key" message; consistent with the known blocked-chat-key situation.
- **Kill vs Stop:** header/console expose Stop/Restart (real `gamePower`); a distinct force-kill (SIGKILL) path isn't wired — Stop is the closest real action.
- Rust uses WebSocket RCON (not wired) so its console command box auto-disables via the action's message; power/logs/schedules still work.
